name: seekpeek_1of16_bridge

phase_0.boundary_condition: The 12-slot Shavian tuple lattice closed under the fixed 1/16 winding bridge. A public key enters, its bg frame is computed by per-slot SHA256 draws, the bridge advances six positions to yield the hqe frame, and un_bridge returns the fixed glyphs to their canonical pre-images, recovering the bg frame exactly. Nothing leaves the lattice and no external store is consulted.

VINIT.justification: the pipeline opens with the raw hex before any slot is named; this is the void state

TANCH.justification: the angle brackets close the system; every glyph lives inside the tuple

AFWD.chosen_element: the 1/16 winding bridge from bg to hqe
AFWD.justification: forward morphism advancing the frame at positions 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 toward the SK-imscribed target

AREV.chosen_element: un_bridge, the inverse winding from hqe to bg
AREV.justification: reverse descent returning fixed glyphs to their canonical pre-images

CLINK.justification: sequential composition of twelve slot draws, each a hash of the public key with its slot label

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the recovered hqe frame as self-identity
IMSCRIB.justification: the frame is itself the SK object this pipeline defines; self-reference without transformation

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the branch of the bg frame into identity and bridge
FSPLIT.justification: the bg frame splits into the identity branch holding bg and the bridge branch holding hqe, where hqe is the 1/16 winding of bg

FFUSE.justification: the inverse winding folds the bridge branch back into the identity branch, reconstituting the split input exactly

EVALT.chosen_element: the loop closure check un_bridge(hqe) == bg
EVALT.justification: affirmative state: the frame loop closes and the recovered frame is emitted as the original SK object

EVALF.chosen_element: the loop-open verdict for an off-canonical bg frame
EVALF.justification: negative state: a bridge position that already held its fixed glyph breaks invertibility; the frame is reported as-is, never as an original

ENGAGR.chosen_element: the two-object duality held at once
ENGAGR.justification: the frame is recovered from the public key alone while the ECC scalar sk*G==P stays possession-gated; both claims are held without resolution

IFIX.chosen_element: the audit trail of scalars verified this run
IFIX.justification: permanent append-only record of supplied or minted scalars; the recovered frame needs no store

split_outputs: bg tuple held on the identity branch
hqe tuple produced by the 1/16 winding bridge of bg

phase_3.void_description: 00: the public key hex before any slot draw; no glyph assigned
phase_3.true_description: 01: the loop closed, un_bridge(hqe) == bg, and the recovered frame emitted as the original SK object
phase_3.false_description: 10: the loop open, an off-canonical bg at a bridge position; nothing emitted as original, nothing fabricated
phase_3.both_description: 11: the duality held at once; the frame is recovered from the public key alone while the ECC scalar sk*G==P remains unobtained

steps.domain_action: the public key hex enters as an unassigned point, nothing named yet
the 12-slot Shavian frame bounds the system, every glyph to live inside the angle brackets
the per-slot SHA256 draws chain across all twelve slots, composing the deterministic bg imscription
the 1/16 winding bridge advances the frame forward at positions 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11
the bg frame branches into the identity branch holding bg and the bridge branch holding hqe
the true arm affirms that hqe is a pure function of the public key, recomputable by any holder
the hqe frame recognizes itself as the SK object this pipeline defines
the false arm descends the inverse winding, returning fixed glyphs to their canonical pre-images
the false arm rejects an off-canonical bg whose bridge positions already held fixed glyphs, marking the loop open
un_bridge(hqe) folds back into bg, the fused result equal to the split input
the loop closure is affirmed, un_bridge(hqe) == bg == imscription(P)
the two-object duality is held, the frame recovered from the key alone and the ECC scalar still possession-gated
the audit trail records only scalars verified this run; the recovered frame needs no store
the system closes; nothing left the tuple lattice and no registry was consulted

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the per-slot SHA256 imscription translating the public key hex into the bg tuple, and the fixed bridge translating bg into hqe
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: tuple passing across the 12-slot frame; each slot carries one Shavian glyph and the bridge positions communicate their shift by overwrite
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the bg and hqe frames in the tuple lattice; the audit file holds only scalars verified in this run
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: deterministic order: imscribe the public key, bridge the bg frame, then evaluate the loop closure before any emission
phase_5.alfs_store: the secp256k1 curve parameters with generator G and order q, together with the seekpeek bridge_tool implementation as the bootstrap store

phase_6.cycle_cost: one SHA256 draw per slot and one fixed glyph overwrite per bridge position
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: the public key hex with its bg frame uncomputed
phase_6.post_cycle_state: the bg frame, the hqe frame, and the closure verdict un_bridge(hqe) == bg
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the frame transformation is deterministic and the loop closes exactly, so no information is created or destroyed

banked_count_check.verdict: 1 unit(s) survived a clear by being banked in a frame (1 live clear(s))
